clue.text: Perhaps broadcast at such top tennis player's occasion?

parts.note: a seed is a highly ranked player in a tennis draw
an occasion is a time, as in 'on that time'

explanation.surface: A question about some big event for a leading tennis star, perhaps shown on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like television, but here it is scattering seed by hand, and the definition asks for the season when that is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting is a way of sowing, done in the sowing season of the farming year.

clue.text: Two seasons when floods are likely?

parts.note: spring is a season of the year
tide is an old word for a season, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: A question about times of year when flooding happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tide' meaning season survives in Eastertide and Yuletide.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring tide is an unusually high tide at new and full moon, bringing a risk of flooding.

clue.text: Old alcoholic drink in bond which gets people worked up

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the bond word

parts.note: cement bonds things together
it is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A vintage tipple in a trust fund that riles people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' for Italian vermouth is an old bar term (gin and it).
explanation.definitionFit: Excitement is a state of agitation or thrill.

clue.text: One attempts to locate German city

explanation.surface: Someone tries to find a place in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who has a go; Trier is an old city on the Moselle.

clue.text: A trick of the light?

parts.note: a conjuring act done with light, an early slide projector that cast images on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: An early projector made images appear by shining a lamp through painted slides, an illusion of light.

clue.text: Hope for a high church position?

parts.note: a spire is the tall point placed high on a church

explanation.surface: Someone longs to rise to a senior post in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High church position' reads like a bishopric, but it is the literal steeple on top of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope for something is to set one's sights on it, to strive towards it.

clue.text: Country people will take time to make a report

parts.note: a state is a country
men means people

explanation.surface: Folk from a nation take a moment to file an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal account or declaration.

clue.text: Strong sarcasm must be cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the sarcasm word is dropped

parts.note: irony is sarcasm

explanation.surface: Harsh mockery should be kept brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron as an adjective means firm and unyielding, as in an iron will.

clue.text: It's simple to have some ideas yourself

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Coming up with a few thoughts on your own is no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy is straightforward, needing little effort.

clue.text: Severe grillings of car organisation's leaders

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation
kings are leaders of their nations

explanation.surface: Bosses of a motoring club face tough questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British breakdown and motoring club, like the AA.
explanation.definitionFit: Racking is putting under torture, so rackings are harsh interrogations or ordeals.

clue.text: What passengers pay to go round ring of islands

indicators.note: go round means the fare word encircles the ring letter

parts.note: passengers pay fares to travel
a ring is round in shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: Travellers' payments cover a circular trip round an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' puts O inside FARES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faroes are a North Atlantic archipelago between Shetland and Iceland.

clue.text: Nervous desciption of alpine violin maker's work?

definitions.text: desciption of alpine violin maker's work?

explanation.surface: A tense luthier working in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Alpine is high up, and a violin maker's finished work is strung.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly-strung means tense and excitable; read literally it is strings fitted up a mountain.

clue.text: This eliminates gross errors of cricket?

definitions.text: This eliminates gross errors of cricket?

parts.words: This eliminates gross errors of cricket?
parts.note: gross is the opposite of net, and the session in the nets at a cricket ground is where batters iron out their mistakes

explanation.surface: Something that removes blatant blunders from a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' reads as 'glaring', but its opposite in accounts is 'net', and cricket nets are where players practise.
explanation.definitionFit: Training in the nets is how cricketers rehearse strokes to cut out their mistakes.

clue.text: Astronomers make use of these short and long times

parts.note: light means short of weight, as in a light measure
years are long stretches of time

explanation.surface: Astronomers deal in both brief and lengthy periods.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests units of time, but the answer is a unit of distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers measure stellar distances in the distance light travels in a year.

clue.text: Attendants see shutter put in place

indicators.note: put in place means arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Ushers watch a window cover being fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in place' rearranges SEE SHUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Usherettes were women who showed patrons to seats in cinemas and theatres.

clue.text: Afraid, and stupid with it, on retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: dim means stupid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scared and slow-witted, about to step back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns DIMIT into TIMID; it also hints at shyness, which suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person is nervous and easily frightened.

clue.text: One's bound to get worn down given wimp's manner

definitions.text: One's bound to get worn down

parts.note: a drip is a feeble person, a wimp
tone means manner, as in tone of voice

explanation.surface: A feeble person's way of talking is sure to wear people out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint at stone eroded by dripping water.
explanation.definitionFit: A dripstone is rock formed by dripping water, or a moulding where rainwater runs off.

clue.text: His cattle could be running?

indicators.note: could be says these letters may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A farmer's herd might be stampeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HIS CATTLE; 'running' looks like the cows' action but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Running is one example of a track and field sport.

clue.text: Small cavity is test for this discipline?

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow
to try is to test

explanation.surface: A little hole is the exam for this field of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavity' hints at teeth, which suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentistry is a professional field of medicine, the care of teeth.

clue.text: Man in support of golfer gives a laugh

indicators.note: in places the man word inside the golf support word

parts.note: a tee holds the golf ball up for the first shot
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A caddie helping a golfer chuckles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support of golfer' looks like a caddie, but is the peg the ball sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is a giggle, a small snigger.

clue.text: Start off hard by river in Scottish district

indicators.note: off means out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the Clyde is the river through Glasgow

explanation.surface: Begin an outing in difficult conditions by a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges START into STRAT. Strathclyde was a Scottish region around Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Strathclyde was a local government region of west Scotland.

clue.text: Bird is able to fly round river

indicators.note: fly round means the ability word circles about the river

parts.note: can means is able
the Po is a river in Italy

explanation.surface: A bird that can fly around a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

clue.text: Please play violin soundly and another instrument

indicators.note: soundly signals the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an entreaty to bow a violin is 'O bow!'

explanation.surface: A request to bow the violin alongside a second instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' is an old poetic 'please', and bowing is how a violin is played.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Tailless animal in porch

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the animal word is removed

parts.note: a stoat is a small weasel-like animal

explanation.surface: A creature without a tail sits in a porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Frog, however, has not returned

parts.note: but means however

indicators.note: returned means the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: An amphibian that has failed to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes TON. A frog is also an ornamental coat fastening, the sense needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is a decorative braided fastening on a coat, used in place of a stud.

clue.text: One leaves suitor to take over

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for one departs from the suitor word

parts.note: a suppliant is a suitor, one who makes a humble plea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lover walks out and someone else moves in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suitor' reads as a wooer, but here means a petitioner.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant is to replace or oust someone from their place.

clue.text: Paint celebrity in the Spanish style

indicators.note: in places the celebrity word inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Depict a famous person in the manner of a Spanish artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' only finishes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy paint giving a hard finish.

clue.text: Worries about noise gas is making

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets over what the gas is making noise about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NOISE GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to fret, to suffer anguish over something.
